abstract: Kernel-checked certificates for the multiplicative compositum of the two registered Mahler minimizers — rho, the real root of x^3 = x + 1 (the plastic number: Smyth's nonreciprocal minimum, Siegel's smallest Pisot number) and Q, the real root > 1 of x^4 = x + 1 (the degree-4 entry of the minimal-measure tables) — together with the Bedford-Kim spectral family whose limit rho is, and (new in version 2) the identification of that family with the Coxeter-element spectra of the E_m star trees. Twenty-two compared theorems. The spectral half: (1) for n >= 7 the family chi_n(x) = x^(n+1)(x^3 - x - 1) + (x^3 + x^2 - 1) has a canonical root in [117/100, rho), largest below rho, strictly increasing, tending to rho; (2) every chi_n is strictly positive on [rho, infinity); (3) chi_7 = (x - 1) * L exactly, over any commutative ring, with L Lehmer's degree-10 polynomial; (4) L has a root in [117/100, rho). The compositum half, for the degree-12 minimal polynomial of rho * Q (written out in full in every compared statement): (5) an exclusion witness — a nonreal quartic root z with 1 < |rho * z| < rho * Q; (6) the twelve embedding products ARE the conjugates of rho * Q, both directions; (7) there are exactly twelve of them; (8) rho * Q is an algebraic unit, via an explicit degree-11 cofactor over any commutative ring — the (3, 4, 12) triple in the normal form alpha * beta * gamma = 1; (9) the degree-12 polynomial is not reciprocal (neither its reversal nor the reversal's negation), placing it in the regime of Smyth's theorem; (10) degree multiplicativity — deg minpoly(rho*Q) = deg minpoly(rho) * deg minpoly(Q) = 12; (11) the compositum in sup form Q(rho) join Q(Q) = Q(rho*Q), of degree 12, with the two simple extensions linearly disjoint; (12) the complete unit-circle census — EXACTLY 5 conjugates strictly outside, EXACTLY 7 strictly inside, NONE on the circle, so rho * Q is neither a Pisot nor a Salem number; (13) the house — every conjugate other than rho * Q has modulus strictly below rho * Q; (14) the exact Mahler measure M = rho^2 * Q^2 * psi, where psi is the real root > 1 of psi^4 = psi^3 + 1; (15) the registry bridge — M(X^4 - X - 1) = psi and M(rulerPoly) = (rho * Q)^2 * M(X^4 - X - 1), re-proving in-repo the quantity pinned in registered entry PALOMAR-2026-08-31-000004; (16) the order-12 Hadamard product recurrence — the termwise product of any solutions of the cubic and quartic shift recurrences satisfies the order-12 recurrence whose characteristic polynomial is exactly the degree-12 polynomial, in any Q-algebra; (17) the annihilator ideal of the product power sequence n |-> (rho * Q)^n is EXACTLY the principal ideal of the degree-12 polynomial — the classical order <= 3 * 4 bound is an equality, forced by the polynomial's kernel-held irreducibility. THE COXETER BRIDGE (version 2), for the star trees E_m = T(2,3,m-3) with generalized Cartan matrix A given entrywise and Coxeter element c = s_0 s_1 ... s_{m-1}, each simple reflection the matrix s_i = 1 - e_i e_i^T A of the geometric representation: (18) for every m >= 4, (X - 1) * charpoly(c) = X^(m-2)(X^3 - X - 1) + (X^3 + X^2 - 1) — the classical E_n Coxeter-polynomial identity (recorded in Gross-Hironaka-McMullen 2009, Section 1, and proved there as Cor. 4.3 for n >= 4), whose right-hand side is chi_{m-3}: the spectral half of this entry IS the E_m Coxeter spectrum; (19) with the E_10 Cartan matrix written out, the Coxeter polynomial of E_10 is Lehmer's polynomial; (20) for every m >= 10 the Coxeter polynomial of E_m has a root lambda_m in [117/100, rho) with no real root above it, the lambda_m strictly increasing and tending to rho; (21) for every m >= 10 the complexified Coxeter element has an eigenvalue lambda in (1, rho) and every complex eigenvalue is unimodular, lambda, or 1/lambda; (22) that lambda dominates the modulus of every eigenvalue and is a Salem number, for every m >= 10, with the Salem predicate written out as in the registered entry PALOMAR-2026-09-02-000003. Two disclosures of version 1 are discharged by (21)-(22) for n >= 7: the Salem property of the Bedford-Kim roots is now kernel-held, and the interval (1, 117/100) is now swept (the only eigenvalues off the unit circle are lambda_m and its inverse). The results address four research audiences: the degree problem for products and composita of algebraic numbers (the certified (3,4,12) witness at a canonically distinguished pair, in the field's own unit-product normal form); the Mahler-measure tradition (the measure of the composed product of the two degree-minimal polynomials, in closed form in the second-smallest Pisot number); composed products of polynomials (a certified rational instance where the finite-field coprimality criterion is unavailable and irreducibility is proved by elimination); and, new, Coxeter groups and Salem numbers (McMullen; Gross-Hironaka-McMullen; Hironaka's Lehmer program): the E_m Coxeter spectra, their Salem radii and their limit rho as one kernel-checked family — with the Lean audience served by concrete exercise of the Mahler-measure, linear-disjointness, Matrix.charpoly and spectrum APIs. Like the golden ratio, rho * Q is an algebraic unit of norm -1; the compared cofactor identity is that norm computation, certified. No novelty claim is made for the measure identity (the entry is not aware of it in the literature; the claimed contribution is the kernel certificate), none for the mathematics of (18)-(22), which is classical (the claimed contribution is the kernel-checked bridge from the registered Bedford-Kim family to the E_m Coxeter elements, for every m >= 4 (bridge) and every m >= 10 (spectrum, Salem) at once), no "first formalization" claim is made anywhere, and whether rho is ATTAINED as a dynamical degree is open in the literature — no statement claims it. Hypotheses are inline: rho, Q, psi enter only through their defining equations plus root-selection inequalities, the E_m Cartan matrices only through their entries, and the compared statements use only core Mathlib vocabulary (Filter.Tendsto, nhds, the complex norm, minpoly, Polynomial.rootSet, Set.ncard, Polynomial.mahlerMeasure, IntermediateField adjoin/sup, Module.finrank, Finset.range sums, Matrix.charpoly, Matrix.diagonal, List.finRange/List.prod, matrix literals, Matrix.map, spectrum, IsIntegral, Polynomial.aeval) — zero custom definitions. The name prefix "ruler" in statement names is the source project's term for the product rho * Q; nothing in any statement depends on it.

related_formalizations.note: The compared statements use only core Mathlib vocabulary — zero custom definitions on the compared surface. Mathlib contains no Salem numbers, no Lehmer polynomial, no Pisot theory, no Coxeter elements or Coxeter polynomials of generalized Cartan matrices, and no Hadamard-product theory for linear recurrences (checked at the pin): the family, the compositum certificates, the census, the exact measure evaluations, the minimal product recurrence, and the Coxeter bridge are this entry's contribution. Mathlib's Polynomial.mahlerMeasure, IntermediateField.LinearDisjoint.of_finrank_coprime (disclosed as near-automating the disjointness half of statement (11)), Matrix.charpoly and spectrum are consumed.

related_formalizations.identifier: Registered entry PALOMAR-2026-08-31-000004 (stalex444/mahler-measure-minima, registered revision ca3df22)
related_formalizations.note: The registered sibling entry that kernel-certifies the pair's selection: for each degree d in {2, 3, 4}, x^d - x - 1 attains the minimal Mahler measure among monic irreducible integer polynomials of degree d with measure above one, with the minima pinned exactly (M^3 = M + 1 at degree 3; M^4 = M^3 + 1 at degree 4). Compared statement (15) re-proves that entry's degree-4 quantity in-repo as the left conjunct of (15); the values match: M(X^4 - X - 1) = psi and M(rulerPoly) = (rho * Q)^2 * M(X^4 - X - 1). The selection of the pair (rho, Q) is therefore the literature's and the registry's, not this entry's. The module PdtPisotBoundary carried here is identical, apart from the module-system header, to the module of the same name in that entry and in PALOMAR-2026-09-04-000004 (stalex444/chiral-padovan-histories, registered revision 14711e6).

The registered Salem entry whose Salem predicate compared statement (22) writes out verbatim, and whose certificate modules PdtSalemCircle, PdtSalemArith, PdtSalemMinus, PdtPisotLadder and PdtSalemEndgame are carried here unchanged apart from the module-system header (they built on Lean 4.35.0-rc2 without repair). Statement (22) composes that entry's minus-family trichotomy with the bridge (18) and the plastic pattern of the family.

The broader public project this entry belongs to. This repository is the complete, self-contained proof development for the compared statements, not a wrapper: every proof module builds here with the pinned toolchain and no imports from the parent. PdtIrreducible, PdtSalemFamily and PdtRulerMinpoly descend from material in the parent development at the pinned revision; PdtRulerCensus, PdtRulerMeasure and PdtRulerRecurrence are native to this repository; PdtStarDet, PdtCoxElt, PdtCoxeterBridge and PdtCoxeterSpectral were written for version 2 and appear in no other development; PdtSalemPlasticPattern is a trimmed copy (the plastic-pattern lines only, verbatim, plus rho_real_root_unique copied verbatim from PdtMahlerWindow of the public parent) of a module of the author's unpublished development — the source module is not public, so the trim is disclosed rather than externally checkable; every line of it is kernel-checked in this build, and the trim is stated in its docstring.
